title: A New Song of Praise
overview: Psalm 98 is a jubilant call to worship, celebrating God's marvelous deeds, especially His salvation and righteous judgment. This psalm invites all the earth to sing a new song to the Lord, recognizing His victory and faithfulness toward Israel and all nations. It emphasizes joyful praise through music and the natural world’s participation in worship, culminating in the anticipation of God’s righteous judgment over the earth. Positioned within the Psalter, Psalm 98 highlights God’s universal kingship and the global scope of His salvation, encouraging believers to respond with exuberant worship and trust in His justice.
structure:
**Verses 1-3: The Call to Praise for God’s Marvelous Works.** The psalm opens with an invitation to sing a new song because of God’s victorious acts, His revealed salvation, and His faithfulness to Israel, witnessed by all nations. 

**Verses 4-6: The Call for Joyful Musical Praise.** The psalmist exhorts all the earth to make joyful noise, sing, and rejoice with various instruments, emphasizing the communal and celebratory nature of worship.

**Verses 7-9: The Cosmic Celebration and Divine Judgment.** The psalm concludes by calling on the sea, floods, and hills to join in joyful praise as God comes to judge the earth with righteousness and equity, highlighting His sovereign rule over all creation.

keyVerses.text: O sing unto the LORD a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory.
keyVerses.significance: This verse sets the tone for the entire psalm, emphasizing the reason for new praise: God's marvelous deeds and victorious power. It underscores God's active role in salvation history and invites believers to respond with fresh worship.

keyVerses.text: He hath remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel: all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights God's faithfulness to Israel and the universal revelation of His salvation, pointing to the global impact of God's redemptive work and the fulfillment of His covenant promises.

keyVerses.text: With trumpets and sound of cornet make a joyful noise before the LORD, the King.
keyVerses.significance: This verse emphasizes the use of music and instruments in worship, celebrating God’s kingship. It reflects the biblical theme of rejoicing before the sovereign Lord with exuberant praise.

keyVerses.text: Before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity.
keyVerses.significance: This verse anticipates the righteous judgment of God over all the earth, affirming His justice and fairness. It connects worship with the hope and assurance of God’s righteous governance.

characters.name: The LORD
characters.description: God is the central figure in this psalm, portrayed as the victorious King who accomplishes marvelous deeds, reveals salvation, remembers mercy and truth, and judges the earth with righteousness and equity.

characters.name: The Earth and Creation
characters.description: Personified as participants in worship, the earth, sea, floods, and hills are called to rejoice and make joyful noise, symbolizing all creation’s recognition of God’s sovereign rule and salvation.

themes.description: The psalm emphasizes singing a new song to the Lord, symbolizing fresh and renewed worship in response to God’s ongoing mighty acts, a theme that resonates throughout Scripture as a call to celebrate God’s redemptive work.
The revelation of God’s salvation to all nations highlights the universal scope of His redemptive plan, affirming that God’s mercy and truth extend beyond Israel to the ends of the earth.
The psalm underscores the importance of joyful, musical praise using various instruments, reflecting the biblical tradition of worship as a vibrant, communal celebration of God’s kingship.
The concluding verses focus on God’s righteous judgment over the earth, assuring believers of His just governance and the ultimate establishment of equity among peoples.

historicalContext: Psalm 98 likely originates from the post-exilic period when Israel was restored from Babylonian captivity, a time marked by renewed hope and worship centered on God’s faithfulness and salvation. The psalm reflects the cultural practice of using music and public celebration in worship, common in ancient Israelite religious life. Geographically, it addresses the entire earth and creation, consistent with Israel’s expanding understanding of God’s universal reign. Politically, the psalm contrasts God’s righteous kingship with earthly rulers, offering assurance of divine justice amid uncertain human governance.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology sees Psalm 98 as a proclamation of God’s sovereign salvation and righteous judgment, emphasizing God’s covenant faithfulness to His people and the call for believers to respond in joyful obedience and worship.

Dispensational interpreters often view this psalm as prophetic of Christ’s second coming, where the new song and cosmic rejoicing anticipate the millennial reign of Christ and His righteous judgment over the earth.

Early Church Fathers interpreted Psalm 98 typologically, seeing the new song as the praise of the Church for Christ’s redemptive work and the cosmic elements as symbolic of the new creation in Christ.

crossReferences.connection: This verse also calls for a new song to the Lord, linking the theme of fresh praise to God’s mighty acts of salvation.
The new song in Revelation echoes Psalm 98’s call to worship God for His redemptive victory through the Lamb.
Psalm 96 similarly calls for singing a new song to the Lord for His marvelous works, reinforcing the theme of joyful worship.
This passage includes a call for all creation to rejoice before the Lord, paralleling Psalm 98’s cosmic call to worship.
Paul quotes Psalm 98 to emphasize praising God among the Gentiles, highlighting the universal scope of God’s salvation.

application: Regularly offer God new and heartfelt praise, recognizing His ongoing work in your life.
Trust in God’s righteous judgment as a source of hope amid injustice and uncertainty.
Engage in joyful worship using music and communal celebration to honor God’s kingship.
Remember and proclaim God’s mercy and truth, sharing the message of salvation with others.
Recognize that all creation is called to worship God, inspiring reverence for His sovereign rule.
conclusion: Psalm 98 remains a powerful invitation for believers to celebrate God’s marvelous salvation and righteous judgment with fresh, joyful worship. It unites themes of God’s faithfulness, universal kingship, and the cosmic scope of praise, encouraging Christians to respond with exuberant music and trust in His just governance. This psalm inspires confidence in God’s redemptive plan and calls the church to proclaim His mercy and truth to all the earth.

definitions.definition: A fresh, inspired hymn of praise acknowledging new acts of God’s salvation and faithfulness.
A biblical symbol of power and victory, representing God’s mighty intervention on behalf of His people.
A brass wind instrument used in ancient Israelite worship to produce joyful sounds during praise.
Fairness and justice in judgment, reflecting God’s impartial and righteous governance.

outline.heading: Call to Sing a New Song
outline.description: The psalmist invites all to sing a new song celebrating God’s marvelous deeds, salvation, and faithfulness to Israel, witnessed by all nations.

outline.heading: Exhortation to Joyful Musical Praise
outline.description: A call for the whole earth to rejoice with loud singing and musical instruments, honoring the Lord as King.

outline.heading: Cosmic Praise and Divine Judgment
outline.description: Creation is personified to join in joyful praise as God comes to judge the earth with righteousness and equity, affirming His sovereign rule.
